title: The arrow keys step by the grid while the grid is pulling
goal: With the grid on and Snap to grid on, dragging a layer lands it on grid lines but nudging it with the arrow keys still moves it by one point, so the two ways of moving something disagree and a nudged layer walks off the grid it was just put on.
notes: Found while building the-grid-is-always-behind-the-canvas-and-things on 2026-09-05. Nudge.swift in PhotonzCore holds the step; CanvasGridSettings.snapSpacing is the grid step to use. TDD in core.
acceptance: With Snap to grid on, an arrow key moves a layer by one grid step
Shift and an arrow key moves it by a larger multiple of the grid, not by ten points
With the grid off, or Snap to grid off, the arrow keys behave exactly as they do today
A layer that is already off the grid comes back onto it on the first nudge rather than staying off by the same amount

log.note: Note from 2026-09-05: CanvasGridSettings.snapSpacing is now a function, snapSpacing(atZoom:), because the pull follows the lines being drawn at the current zoom. A nudge has no zoom of its own, so this task has a question to answer that it did not have before: an arrow key should almost certainly step by the same thing a drag lands on, which means reading the canvas's zoom (CanvasView.canvasSnapSpacing already does exactly that) rather than the typed spacing.
